### 2B — International peace, restraint, lawful security

- `THA2023R3-2B-01` — Cobra Gold 2023 opened in Thailand on 28 February. The official U.S. Indo-Pacific Command account describes it as Thai-U.S. co-sponsored, involving integrated land, sea, air, space, humanitarian, and disaster-response activity. This is direct evidence of institutional security cooperation during Prayut’s tenure, but not a personal Prayut decision. Lenses: 2B.7, 2B.8, 2B.10. [INDOPACOM release](https://www.pacom.mil/Media/News/Article/3312746/us-indo-pacific-commander-travels-to-thailand-attends-opening-of-cobra-gold-exe/)

- `THA2023R3-2B-02` — Thailand’s southern peace-dialogue panel and BRN met in Kuala Lumpur on 21–22 February 2023 and agreed to develop a Joint Comprehensive Plan towards Peace for 2023–24, including violence reduction and public consultation. Government-policy attribution is supportable; personal Prayut authorship is not established. Lenses: 2B.1, 2B.4, 2B.7, 2B.10. [Thai Internal Security Operations Command](https://www.southpeace.go.th/?p=70308)

- `THA2023R3-2B-03` — The same official account records that technical working groups were tasked to draft the plan during March–May 2023 for consideration at the June dialogue. This is a distinct implementation step rather than merely a meeting record. Attribution remains to the Thai peace-process apparatus, not personally to Prayut. Lenses: 2B.4, 2B.7, 2B.8. [Thai Internal Security Operations Command](https://www.southpeace.go.th/?p=70308)

- `THA2023R3-2B-04` — AP reported that Cobra Gold 2023 included 7,394 participants and humanitarian, disaster-relief, command-post, and field-training components. This corroborates the official account and provides contrary/mitigating evidence against treating all Thai military activity as coercive or escalatory. Lenses: 2B.7, 2B.8, 2B.10. [AP](https://apnews.com/article/physical-fitness-united-states-government-thailand-e88e05d546ca3d66018e53601dc4c94c)

- `THA2023R3-2B-05` — The December 2023 Chiang Rai clash in which Thai soldiers killed 15 suspected drug smugglers and seized over two million methamphetamine tablets is retained as post-handover context only; it cannot be attributed to Prayut. Lenses: 2B.4, 2B.8. [AP](https://apnews.com/article/thailand-methamphetamine-bust-cf425caad7f39378f767ac8911a5c539)

### 3B — Domestic safety, restraint, protection

- `THA2023R3-3B-01` — Amnesty reported in January 2023 that authorities had revoked bail for two young activists and were arbitrarily detaining people prosecuted for peaceful expression. This is a contemporaneous independent corroboration of the detention/bail pattern, though it does not identify a Prayut instruction. Lenses: 3B.1, 3B.5, 3B.8. [Amnesty International](https://www.amnesty.org/en/documents/asa39/6389/2023/en/)

- `THA2023R3-3B-02` — Amnesty’s July 2023 case report states that a child protester faced Article 112 and other charges arising from a peaceful satirical protest, and that 286 children had faced criminal charges connected to protests by 11 July 2023. Period fit is strong; attribution is to authorities during Prayut’s government, not to a documented personal order. Lenses: 3B.1, 3B.5, 3B.7, 3B.8. [Amnesty International](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2023/07/thailand-drop-insulting-the-monarchy-charge-against-child-protester-involved-in-mock-fashion-show/)

- `THA2023R3-3B-03` — A June 2023 UN Special Procedures communication recorded charges against four protesters following the 2022 APEC protest and cited Thailand’s National Human Rights Commission finding excessive police force. The initiating conduct was pre-period, while the charges and communication were in 2023; it should remain temporally split. Lenses: 3B.2, 3B.4, 3B.7, 3B.9. [OHCHR communication](https://spcommreports.ohchr.org/TMResultsBase/DownLoadPublicCommunicationFile?gId=28446)

- `THA2023R3-3B-04` — Amnesty documented that Thai authorities had failed to protect children during protests and that violent arrests, unlawful detention, intimidation, and surveillance affected young protesters. This is pattern evidence from an independent source, not direct evidence of Prayut’s personal instruction. Lenses: 3B.1, 3B.5, 3B.8, 3B.10. [Amnesty International](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2023/07/thailand-drop-insulting-the-monarchy-charge-against-child-protester-involved-in-mock-fashion-show/)

### 4B — Political freedom versus authoritarian rule

- `THA2023R3-4B-01` — Thailand’s Election Commission certified all 500 elected MPs on 19 June 2023. It stated that certification proceeded even though fraud investigations were incomplete, while preserving the possibility of later Supreme Court challenges. This is direct institutional evidence of election administration and a contrary qualification against describing the process as wholly noncompetitive. Lenses: 4B.1, 4B.2, 4B.8. [Thai Government PRD report](https://thailand.prd.go.th/en/content/category/detail/id/48/iid/190994)

- `THA2023R3-4B-02` — The ECT’s preliminary results recorded Move Forward first in the party-list vote with 14,233,895 votes and reported 75.2% turnout. This supports electoral competitiveness and voter participation, without implying that Prayut personally enabled or obstructed the result. Lenses: 4B.1, 4B.2, 4B.10. [Thai Government PRD report](https://thailand.prd.go.th/en/content/category/detail/id/48/iid/181946)

- `THA2023R3-4B-03` — On 19 July, Parliament voted that Pita could not be renominated under parliamentary rules; Nation Thailand reports 395 of 715 votes in favor of that interpretation. The item is attributable to the parliamentary majority and includes a United Thai Nation MP among opponents, but does not establish a Prayut instruction. Lenses: 4B.2, 4B.4, 4B.8. [Nation Thailand](https://www.nationthailand.com/thailand/politics/40029514)

- `THA2023R3-4B-04` — In January 2024, the Constitutional Court ruled 8–1 that Pita’s iTV shareholding did not violate the Constitution. This post-period ruling cannot erase the July 2023 suspension, but it is contrary evidence against treating the suspension allegation as ultimately legally substantiated. Lenses: 4B.4, 4B.6, 4B.10. [AP](https://apnews.com/article/fc24957735c693b21988029ebacec5f2)

### 5B — Economic well-being and prosperity

- `THA2023R3-5B-01` — The World Bank’s January 2024 Global Economic Prospects gives Thailand’s 2023 real-GDP growth as 1.9%. This is a direct underlying locator replacing the prior Wikipedia-routed claim. It remains a country-level outcome, not a Prayut-attributed policy result. Lenses: 5B.1, 5B.3, 5B.9, 5B.10. [World Bank GEP PDF](https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099159101082419813/pdf/IDU1079447f81a6f81463a1b235156a74338379b.pdf)

- `THA2023R3-5B-02` — The World Bank reported that 2023 growth was dampened by contracting goods exports and continuing fiscal consolidation. This supplies causal context but not a ruler-specific implementation chain. Lenses: 5B.1, 5B.3, 5B.6, 5B.10. [World Bank](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2023/12/14/thai-economy-to-recover-in-2024-driven-by-tourism-exports-recovery)

- `THA2023R3-5B-03` — Thailand’s BOI recorded 891 investment-promotion applications worth THB 364.42 billion during January–June 2023, including substantial electronics, food-processing, automobile, and EV projects. This is an implementation/output indicator during Prayut’s tenure; personal authorship is not established. Lenses: 5B.3, 5B.6, 5B.7, 5B.9. [Nation Thailand](https://www.nationthailand.com/thailand/economy/40029226)

- `THA2023R3-5B-04` — The IMF reported that Thai authorities remained committed to disciplined public-finance management and fiscal consolidation, while inflation averaged 1.3% in 2023. The December fiscal framework was post-handover and must not be attributed to Prayut, but the macroeconomic policy environment is relevant context. Lenses: 5B.1, 5B.3, 5B.8, 5B.10. [IMF Country Report 24/35](https://www.imf.org/-/media/files/publications/cr/2024/english/1thaea2024001.pdf)

### 6B — Social well-being and human development

- `THA2023R3-6B-01` — NHSO reported that 2023 universal-coverage reforms expanded “outpatient anywhere,” “inpatient anywhere,” and “Cancer Anywhere”; more than 47 million people were covered, with over 1.81 million outpatient-anywhere visits and over two million inpatient transfers. This is a clear 2023 social-service outcome, but institutional attribution is to NHSO and the Ministry of Public Health, not personally to Prayut. Lenses: 6B.1, 6B.3, 6B.5, 6B.8. [NHSO](https://eng.nhso.go.th/view/1/DescriptionNews/UCS-elevated-Throughout-2023/604/EN-US)

- `THA2023R3-6B-02` — NHSO reported new 2023 benefits including hepatitis-B, thalassemia, syphilis, HIV self-testing, BRCA screening, newborn hearing screening, genetic screening, and dental implants. These are distinct policy/output units under the national health system, with indirect ruler attribution. Lenses: 6B.2, 6B.3, 6B.5, 6B.8. [NHSO](https://eng.nhso.go.th/view/1/DescriptionNews/UCS-elevated-Throughout-2023/604/EN-US)

- `THA2023R3-6B-03` — NHSO reported that outpatient visits increased from 167.37 million in 2022 to 170.39 million in 2023 and that HIV-prevention services reached 3.54 million people. This is a measurable social-service outcome, not evidence of Prayut’s personal direction. Lenses: 6B.3, 6B.5, 6B.8. [NHSO](https://eng.nhso.go.th/view/1/DescriptionNews/UCS-elevated-Throughout-2023/604/EN-US)

- `THA2023R3-6B-04` — Thailand’s Promotion of Learning Act B.E. 2566 took effect on 19 May 2023 and elevated non-formal and informal education into a Department of Learning Promotion, including lifelong-learning and public/private cooperation duties. This is a target-period legal reform; the retrieved source does not establish Prayut’s personal authorship. Lenses: 6B.2, 6B.4, 6B.6. [Thai Government](https://thailand.go.th/public/issue-focus-detail/001_06_051?hl=en)

- `THA2023R3-6B-05` — UNDP reports Thailand’s 2022 HDI at 0.803 and inequality-adjusted HDI at 0.681. This remains 2022 contextual evidence, now upgraded to a direct UNDP locator rather than a Wikipedia gateway. Lenses: 6B.8, 6B.10. [UNDP Thailand](https://www.undp.org/thailand/press-releases/thailands-human-development-index-improved-pre-covid-level-yet-more-collective-actions-are-needed-accelerate-progress-finds)

### 7B — Ruler personal integrity and honesty

- `THA2023R3-7B-01` — Thailand’s NACC stated that Prayut and his ministers were required to submit asset-and-liability accounts after leaving office, with submissions due between 6 September and 4 November 2023. This documents an accountability requirement, not compliance, noncompliance, or a finding against Prayut. Lenses: 7B.4, 7B.5, 7B.10. [NACC](https://www.nacc.go.th/categorydetail/2019122712514151207005112EK12853/20230922184733)

- `THA2023R3-7B-02` — The NACC’s April 2023 guidance described anti-corruption and conflict-of-interest prevention measures for government procurement. This is institutional integrity infrastructure, not evidence of Prayut’s personal conduct. Lenses: 7B.4, 7B.5, 7B.10. [NACC](https://www.nacc.go.th/categorydetail/2019122712514151207005112EK12853/20230412103850)

- `THA2023R3-7B-03` — In April 2023, the Supreme Administrative Court ordered the NACC to disclose details of its Prawit luxury-watch investigation. Prawit was Prayut’s deputy PM and former defence minister, but this is adjacent-ruler context and must not be attributed to Prayut personally. Lenses: 7B.4, 7B.6, 7B.10. [Nation Thailand](https://www.nationthailand.com/thailand/politics/40026863)

- `THA2023R3-7B-04` — Targeted searches did not recover an admissible 2023 NACC ruling, asset finding, ombudsman decision, procurement case, recusal event, or disclosure violation involving Prayut personally. This remains an explicit research gap, not a negative evidence item.

### 8B — Ruler effectiveness and competence

- `THA2023R3-8B-01` — The 2023 BOI investment figures provide an observable implementation outcome during the Prayut period: 891 applications worth THB 364.42 billion in the first half of the year, including 14 approved BEV projects worth THB 33.97 billion. Attribution is to BOI/government policy machinery, not directly to Prayut. Lenses: 8B.2, 8B.3, 8B.6, 8B.7. [Nation Thailand](https://www.nationthailand.com/thailand/economy/40029226)

- `THA2023R3-8B-02` — Thailand’s Tourism Authority launched the “Visit Thailand Year 2023” campaign in January, explicitly targeting restored tourist confidence and sustainable tourism. This is a government-agency delivery initiative during Prayut’s tenure; personal PM ownership is not established. Lenses: 8B.2, 8B.5, 8B.7. [TAT](https://www.tatnews.org/2023/01/tat-strengthens-visit-thailand-year-2023-towards-a-meaningful-travel-direction/)

- `THA2023R3-8B-03` — By 15 May 2023, the Thai government reported 9.47 million foreign arrivals and THB 391.78 billion in tourism revenue. This is a target-period recovery outcome and a contrary/mitigating indicator against relying only on weak GDP growth. Attribution remains indirect. Lenses: 8B.3, 8B.6, 8B.7. [Thai Government](https://thailand.go.th/public/event-detail/001_02_398)

- `THA2023R3-8B-04` — The Election Commission’s certification of all 500 MPs on 19 June and the scheduled 14 May election provide precise administrative milestones. These support orderly election execution, while the later parliamentary blockage of Pita remains institution-level evidence requiring separate attribution. Lenses: 8B.1, 8B.2, 8B.5, 8B.8. [Thai Government PRD](https://thailand.prd.go.th/en/content/category/detail/id/48/iid/190994)

- `THA2023R3-8B-05` — The IMF recorded continued fiscal discipline, inflation averaging 1.3%, and gradual monetary normalization in 2023. These are macroeconomic execution outcomes but involve autonomous central-bank and post-handover decisions; they should remain contextual rather than direct Prayut effectiveness evidence. Lenses: 8B.3, 8B.7, 8B.10. [IMF Country Report 24/35](https://www.imf.org/-/media/files/publications/cr/2024/english/1thaea2024001.pdf)

### Disposition changes

- Promote the direct World Bank GEP locator for 2023 GDP growth; demote the Wikipedia-routed duplicate to `context` or `superseded`.
- Promote official INDOPACOM and Thai Internal Security Operations Command items to evidence with institutional, not personal, attribution.
- Promote NHSO, Thai Government Learning Promotion Act, UNDP, Amnesty, and OHCHR items according to the attribution limits above.
- Keep December 2023 border fighting and October 2023 refugee pushbacks as post-handover `context`.
- Keep Prawit’s watch case as adjacent-ruler `context`, not Prayut personal-integrity evidence.
- Keep NACC asset-submission guidance as accountability-system evidence; no Prayut-specific compliance finding was recovered.
- Preserve all Srettha-only economic and post-handover policy items as `context`, never final Prayut evidence.
- Legacy bundled entries should be reconciled against the split canonical keys below.
